- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.4) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for consecutive high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >7% from prior day) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for rebound.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (days 1–7) — apply 10–15% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean-reversion bias in late horizon (days 15–30) — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.2 after 3+ days, reduce forecast by 2–4% to reflect cooling momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — smooth sentiment over 3-day window before adjusting forecast.
